cohort: The study cohort included 555 live births to individuals aged 15-39 years diagnosed with breast, lymphoma, thyroid, melanoma, or gynecological cancer during pregnancy, matched with 2,667 live births to individuals without a cancer diagnosis.
finding: A cancer diagnosis during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of preterm delivery, very preterm delivery, induction of labor, low birth weight, and cesarean delivery, but not with low Apgar score.
mod_finding: Cancer diagnosis during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of induction of labor and cesarean delivery.
